title: Impact of Water Price Increase on Industries and Businesses with High Water Usage and on SMEs' Competitiveness
what_it_is: Impact of Water Price Increase on Industries and Businesses with High Water Usage and on SMEs' Competitiveness

sections.label: Water price rise business costs
sections.summary: The July 2017 water price rise is estimated to raise business costs in chemicals, general manufacturing, accommodation and food services, while agencies help companies cut water usage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The rise in water price since July 2017 is estimated to increase total business costs in the chemicals industry by 0.1%, general manufacturing industry by 0.12%, accommodation industry by 0.17%, and the food services industry by 0.26%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Government agencies have been working with our industry partners to help companies reduce their water usage, which will reduce their water bills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: For instance, the Economic Development Board and the Public Utilities Board (PUB) are working with businesses to implement water efficiency measures and to tap on alternative sources of water, such as seawater, for process cooling.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Businesses looking to improve water efficiency can tap on PUB's Water Efficiency Fund to implement water saving measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: For more customised capability building solutions, including the adoption of water efficiency standards, businesses may tap on Enterprise Singapore's Capability Development Grant, which defrays up to 70% of qualifying project costs.
